brief.headline: Push for a 45→30-day payment term to free up ₹2.25 L of our cash, and benchmark price to the market fair band of ₹0.65–0.80/pc at scale — line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a second source.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for pricing in the ₹0.65–0.80/pc range for higher-volume orders
priceAsk.basis: The open market shows 28 mm PP caps asking ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — we should capture that headroom given our consolidated order size.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹2.25 L of our cash

brief.financialLeverage: Abhinav publishes no financials, so we can't see their profit or cash position. Our ₹27.42 L annual spend is material for a supplier of their size, giving us real negotiating weight. Without their numbers, the smartest play is to use the market benchmarks and credible alternates (Manjushree, Mold-Tek) to set the terms — they need to match the market or risk us qualifying a bigger, proven second source.

evidence.point: We spend ₹27.42 L a year with them on rigid plastic packaging
Cutting payment terms from 45 to 30 days frees up cash for us
The open market for 28 mm PP caps runs ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc
Market shows modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume
HDPE resin import unit value stands at 87.61 ₹/kg, giving us a raw-material baseline

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms — top second-source candidate with scale and stability

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) making pails, containers, pharma packaging — a robust, profitable alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (lead to qualify)
alternates.why: A manufacturer lead from public web research (India-Pan, medium confidence) — verify capability and pricing before sending an RFQ

risks: Abhinav's financials aren't public, so we're flying blind on their health — watch for any signs of cash trouble or capacity strain during the conversation.
Our ₹27.42 L is likely a big piece of their business; if we squeeze too hard without a qualified backup, we risk disrupting supply before we have an alternate onboard.
The market backups (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are leads only — not yet qualified or priced — so don't lean on them as live options until we vet them.
If Abhinav pushes back hard on 30-day terms, they may be cash-tight; in that case, offer to phase the shift (40 days first, then 30) rather than drop the ask entirely.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to lock in a long-term partnership on rigid packaging, and to do that we need pricing in the ₹0.65–0.80 range that the market supports at scale, plus a shift to 30-day payment terms to match our other key suppliers.
